body.estimand_functional: \(\psi(y;x,c)=F_{\rho}(y,\bar c;\bar x;P_{\mathrm{obs}})\big/\sum_{y'\,\text{ in the finite state space of }Y}F_{\rho}(y',\bar c;\bar x;P_{\mathrm{obs}})\) on a successful branch; on a passing affine failure template, \(E_Tq=0\) and \(b_Tq\neq0\) certify nonidentification.

sampling_model.design: One selected observational law \(P(V\mid S=\mathbf 1)\) generated by a positive discrete SCM represented by an input-free COPAG.
sampling_model.units: Identification compares structural models that induce the same complete selected observational distribution.
sampling_model.treatment: The intervention fixes \(X=x\); legal Rule-2 exchanges may reallocate coordinates between \(X\) and \(C\).
sampling_model.overlap: The published positive discrete model class makes every displayed selected conditioning stratum well defined.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: None; the contribution is graphical identification and exact rational certificate synthesis rather than sampling inference.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The selected conditional procedure is sound, while conditional completeness is left to future work.
A sufficient graphical condition and a sound algorithm address \(P_X(Y\mid S=1)\) in one known augmented ADMG with latent variables.
Discrete causal questions reduce to polynomial programs that yield sharp or epsilon-sharp bounds.
Conditional interventional distributions have a necessary-and-sufficient identification criterion for a specified semi-Markovian graph.
CIDP is sound and complete for conditional causal-effect identification from PAGs without selection.
Graphical and formula-specific positivity conditions can license identifying formulas without global strict positivity.

body.tldr: The proposal replaces an overinterpreted isolated-conditioning bow with a reusable exact denominator-lock framework. Branch-sCIDP remains a sound finite formula search. Given a rational interior affine SCM template, a simplex-tangent rank inequality is necessary and sufficient for an exact positive rational pair with the same full selected observational law and selected conditioning denominator but different joint numerators, and the pair is compilable and checkable in polynomial time relative to its explicit encoding. A connected binary construction with \(Y_i\to C_i\) and \(C_i\to S_i\) realizes the lock by tuned informative selection cancellation, yields conditional effects \(9/16\) and \(7/16\), and admits a same-graph perturbation with unequal denominators. Whether every all-branches failure supplies such a forest tangent remains the explicit open question.

project_justification.gap: Selected conditional identification can fail at every joint-identification branch, yet ordinary selected hedges need not preserve the conditioning denominator and an isolated conditioning root makes preservation vacuous.
project_justification.niche: An exact algebraic certificate layer can be useful before full graphical completeness: it must distinguish graph representation, observational-fiber equality, denominator locking, and numerator separation, and it must demonstrate the lock with an informative conditioning variable.
project_justification.fill: The project supplies an if-and-only-if tangent-rank compiler, a complete connected rational witness with a same-graph nonlocking perturbation, and a sharply delimited residual-forest-to-rank question whose resolution would finish formula-or-certificate completeness.

body.related_work: Chen and Mooij provide the selected-COPAG model, complete unconditional sIDP, and sound conditional sCIDP; their work informs the role search and residual-forest handle, but no strict theorem comparison is claimed until the open graph-to-lock step is solved. Abouei and coauthors formulate selected hedges for one known augmented ADMG and an unconditional selected intervention target; their construction informs the forest coordinate but does not address postintervention conditioning or COPAG uncertainty. Duarte and coauthors show that finite discrete causal fibers are polynomially representable and computationally searchable; the present rank system focuses on exact local rational compilation rather than sharp-bound optimization. Shpitser and Pearl give the complete fixed-graph conditional benchmark, and Jaber and coauthors give its no-selection PAG counterpart; both motivate exhaustive exchange before joint identification. Hwang and coauthors motivate formula-specific treatment of positivity and cancellation. Chen, Zoeter, and Mooij provide the selected-SCM semantics used by both members of every certificate.
body.honest_scope: The proposal makes no claim that \(\operatorname{AllFail}\) yields a denominator-locked countermodel. The exact rank equivalence is conditional on a specified rational interior affine mechanism family, and the informative three-observed-variable witness proves nonvacuity rather than completeness. The old isolated \(C_b\) bow is retained only as a regression baseline because its denominator \(1/2\) is structurally automatic. The unresolved open question asks whether simultaneous branch failure entails any such locked construction; no implication in that direction is established here, and failure of one template is not a counterexample. The no-selection specialization must collapse to CIDP. Continuous variables, intervention inputs, generic faithfulness, and finite-alphabet completeness beyond the explicit binary certificate subclass are outside scope.
